per_shot.note: Flat untextured beige wall between two red stripes, black slab ceiling with one faint smudge of light, featureless grey floor; the dusk portholes are the only real mood.
Same flat box; locker and table read as clean primitives but nothing lands light on the wall, and the only floor pool is the suit's own lamp.
Cork board and boxes add a little life, but the shell is still a beige plane with a black lid and a black band under the floor.
Fern and book shelf read clearly; the rug is a plain orange slab with no weave or pattern, and the radio is an unlit grey box with a single dot instead of a glowing dial.
Best frame: the star chart reads instantly and the books add colour, but the arc lamp throws no visible warm pool on wall or floor, so the room is not lit any better than stock.
Bunk is a tan slab with a red block for a pillow, and the kettle and cups are tiny lumps on the counter; the furnished room is only slightly richer than stock.

top_issues.issue: The ceiling is a black void with soft blurred smudges, not a ceiling
top_issues.why: The brief names this as the thing to fix: 'never a black slab'. The top third of every frame is dead black, which makes the room read as a box cut out of the void, not a hab.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Model a low-poly ceiling: ribs continuing the wall pillars, insulated panels between them, a run of conduit, and small practical fixtures whose light falls on the ceiling and upper wall. Keep it darker than the walls, but with readable value and structure.

top_issues.issue: Walls and floor are single flat colours with no material or structure
top_issues.why: Apart from the pillars and two red stripes, the wall is one beige plane and the floor one grey plane. It reads as 'flat beige box', which is exactly the player complaint.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Break the wall into insulated panels with seams and slight value steps between them, add a wainscot or kick plate, conduit runs and a few bolts or vents. Give the floor plating with seams and a darker edge where it meets the wall. Vary value across each surface, not just per object.

top_issues.issue: Light does not land warmly; the only floor pool is the suit's lamp
top_issues.why: The arc lamp, portholes and practicals do not pool on the wall or floor. The room is evenly dim brown, so it reads closer to grim than to the warm lit window of 02-surface. Bought lights should change the room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Have the arc lamp cast a clear warm cone and pool on the floor and wall behind it. Let each porthole throw a soft dusk-orange patch on the floor beneath it. Add small warm practicals (wall sconces or strip lights) with visible pools, and keep the corners and ends darker for contrast.

top_issues.issue: Several bought items do not read as themselves
top_issues.why: The rug is a plain orange slab with no woven pattern; the radio has no glowing dial; the bunk lacks bedding (blanket fold, pillow shape); the kettle and cups are too small to read at play scale. The fern, books and star chart already read well.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Rug: a stepped border and simple geometric pattern in two or three tones. Radio: a warm emissive dial face with a needle that blooms slightly. Bunk: a folded blanket with a turned-down edge, a distinct pillow, a frame or headboard. Galley: a chunkier kettle and cups scaled up to read at play size, maybe with a small warm under-cabinet light.

top_issues.issue: The furnished room is barely richer than the stock room
top_issues.why: Furnishing adds a few props against the same flat, dim shell. Buying things should visibly warm and fill the room, and that is where the reward lives.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Have purchases add light and colour to the room as well as objects: the lamp, radio dial and galley each contribute a warm pool, and the rug and bedding bring pattern and soft colour, so full versus stock is a clear jump in warmth and richness.

protect: The dusk portholes with an orange horizon gradient: the strongest mood element, and they tie the room to 02-surface
The suit is the most legible thing in every frame: white with a cyan visor against warm brown
Fern, book shelf with coloured spines, and the star chart all read clearly as themselves
The low-poly, chunky prop style and the fixed side-view framing
The warm brown/orange family, which places the room on VEIL-3
